findings.title: 5s timeout bounds only the scope close, not the rest of stop(); the comment overclaims
findings.body:
The comment at lines 148-149 says the timeout guarantees the quit path makes progress "even if a backend hangs during teardown". `instance.stop({ timeout })` applies the timeout only inside `closeRun` (`apps/desktop/src/backend/DesktopBackendManager.ts:350-371`, called at line 1087). Three steps in `stop()` run before that and have no limit.

- Line 1051 waits on `mutex.withPermits(1)`. `start` holds the same mutex for its whole body (lines 691-985). That body includes `spec.configResolve`, the filesystem check, and `spec.onPreflightFailed` (lines 784-786). For the primary, `onPreflightFailed` shows a blocking error dialog (`DesktopBackendPool.ts:244-248`).
- Line 1077 calls `spec.onShutdown()`. It is wrapped in `Effect.ignore`, which swallows errors but does not bound time.
- Line 1081 does `Fiber.interrupt(restartFiber)`, which waits for the fiber to finish.

So if the user quits while a `start` is still in the resolve or preflight phase (for example a slow WSL cold boot), the finalizer can wait on the mutex indefinitely. `shutdown.markComplete` then never runs, which is the failure this change is meant to prevent. The exposure is narrower than a hung teardown but real.

If you want a hard guarantee, wrap the whole per-instance `stop` in `Effect.timeoutOption(Duration.seconds(5))` in `stopAllPoolInstances`. Otherwise soften the comment to say the timeout bounds only process-scope teardown.

`DesktopUpdates.ts:599` uses the same `stop({ timeout })` call and has the same gap. Note also that after a timed-out close, `stop()` returns at line 1088 without clearing `active`. The instance's own `Effect.addFinalizer(() => stop())` at line 1157 later calls `stop()` with no timeout. I did not check whether that second `Scope.close` returns immediately on a scope that is already closing.

findings.title: Test covers only the hung-process-teardown case, and relies on timer-registration ordering
findings.body:
The test proves the 5s timeout bounds a hung process-scope finalizer. It does not cover the other unbounded waits in `stop()`: a `start` holding the mutex, or a hung `onShutdown`. Those are the cases that could still stall the quit finalizer (see the finding on `DesktopApp.ts:154`). It also never checks that `shutdown.markComplete` runs, because it tests `stopAllPoolInstances` in isolation and not the `Effect.ensuring` wiring at `DesktopApp.ts:336`.

Separately, the test calls `TestClock.adjust(5s)` as soon as both teardown-started signals arrive. It assumes each instance's `timeoutOption` sleep is registered before the `adjust`. That is likely true, because the registering fiber continues synchronously after `forkIn` while the child is scheduled. It is not asserted anywhere. If the order flips, the test hangs instead of failing cleanly.

contracts.action: Quit finalizer now stops all pool backends with a 5s per-instance timeout (extracted to stopAllPoolInstances) and still marks shutdown complete via Effect.ensuring
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/desktop/src/updates/DesktopUpdates.ts:596-601 (quitAndInstall path) already used instance.stop({ timeout: 5s }) concurrently across pool.list; the old quit finalizer called instance.stop() with no timeout.
contracts.before_after: Before: stop() unbounded, so a hung backend teardown blocked shutdown.markComplete. After: closeRun forks Scope.close(run.scope) into parentScope and awaits it with timeoutOption(5s) (DesktopBackendManager.ts:366-369). On timeout stop() returns early and skips the cleanup of active/telemetry (lines 1088-1090). The close continues in the background. The 2s SIGTERM grace (line 67) is under the 5s budget.
contracts.visible_effect: App quit completes within about 5s of the process-scope close even when a backend does not exit. A backend that outlives the budget may be hard-killed by the OS at app exit.
contracts.failure_mode: Steps before closeRun in stop() (mutex at 1051, onShutdown at 1077, restartFiber interrupt at 1081) are outside the timeout. A quit during an in-flight start (which holds the mutex across preflight and a modal dialog) could still block markComplete indefinitely.

summary: Small, correct refactor: it extracts the quit finalizer into an exported `stopAllPoolInstances` and gives each backend stop a 5s budget, matching the existing `DesktopUpdates` quit path. The new test exercises the timeout through a scope finalizer. One caveat is that the timeout covers only the process-scope close inside `stop()`. The mutex wait, `onShutdown` and the restart-fiber interrupt come before it, so the \"guarantee the quit makes progress\" comment overclaims. The test also leaves those paths and the `markComplete` wiring untested.
